summary: No OWASP-relevant security vulnerabilities found in the two new private helpers (hasPassedDynamicUpstream, partitionWpsAwaitingNextStage). Audit covered: A01 (both helpers unexported — no new public surface), A03 (pure in-memory TypeScript logic — no injection vectors), A04 insecure design (as PipelineType[] | undefined type cast is consistent with the pre-existing module pattern; degraded empty-array paths produce safe fallbacks in resolvePrerequisite and resolveNextAgent), A04 mixed-routing guard ([...nextAgents][0] spread confirmed safe by size===1 pre-check, ?? null nullish-coalescing handles unknown role), A06 (no new dependencies), A08 (no new I/O or deserialization — helpers operate on Zod-validated upstream structs), A10 (no network calls). All acceptance criteria remain met.

comments.note: The 'as PipelineType[] | undefined' cast on wp.active_pipeline_stages in both helpers bypasses TypeScript runtime validation. If a WP has fully invalid stage names, hasPassedDynamicUpstream returns true (vacuously) rather than false — a silent misrouting path. This is consistent with the existing module pattern and the ledger store validates on write, so this is not exploitable. Noted for awareness; no change required.
